first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and is supported by prior durable gains in time-to-value and activation. It also supports the 6% activation decline without accepting the documented 30-day retention risk of promotional pricing. Verify the onboarding evidence and the pricing downside before committing; run a controlled experiment rather than a broad rollout.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment this week. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal. A standard experiment preserves uncertainty about present-day effect size and segment fit.
